extracted.intended_audience: creative writers (especially fiction/speculative fiction) wanting to portray pregnancy and motherhood
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for portraying pregnancy, childbirth, and motherhood in fiction: what writers commonly get wrong and practical suggestions (details, diversity of experience, research/consulting experts, historical/medical accuracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Erasure of pregnancy and motherhood
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancies, children, and motherhood often disappear from fiction, even from background scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make motherhood visible in your stories and backgrounds rather than omitting it; include mothers and children in scenes instead of treating them as absent or dead by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid monstrous-allegory depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancies are often depicted like Alien — a monster taking over your body and emerging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't reduce pregnancy to a horror-allegory by default; acknowledge real risks like maternal mortality when relevant, but balance that with the mundane and managed aspects of many pregnancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pedestal/Messianic depiction of mothers
rubrics_metrics.description: The opposite extreme is putting the mother on a pedestal (holy birth/Messiah) where she 'can do no wrong.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray mothers as flawed, complex people who sometimes screw up and sometimes do well; avoid flattening them into idealized figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show variability between pregnancies and mothers
rubrics_metrics.description: No two pregnancies or parenting experiences are identical; personal experience varies widely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't present a single pregnancy experience as universal; show variation across people and pregnancies and avoid generalizing from one example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include small, specific physical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Small, specific details signal authenticity: baby moving, organs shifting back into place, cautious standing/waddling, the weight and balance changes late in pregnancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sensory details (e.g., feeling the baby kick, the first breath, the sensation when organs shift back) to convey realism; such details indicate research or lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic depiction of labor duration and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor often takes hours (especially first births); it is not usually the 'five-minute' event movies show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray labor as a process that can be long and variable; show waiting, send-home moments when not dilated enough, and realistic timelines to avoid compressing everything into an implausibly short scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray small, common pregnancy problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancy involves many minor, common issues (vitamin shortages, cramps, dietary changes) that are often omitted or flattened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotidian complications (e.g., needing certain foods, cramps from deficiencies) to make the experience believable instead of only showing catastrophes or smooth, effortless pregnancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do research and consult subject-matter experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to real experts in your life (physicians, mothers, midwives, historians) rather than assuming; this will not make you an expert but will broaden your understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a list of subject-matter experts you know and interview them about specifics; use their input for realistic details and to avoid stereotyping or errors (podcast 'homework' advice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid single-facet characterization of mothers
rubrics_metrics.description: People are not single-facet entities; motherhood is one aspect of a person's life, not their entire identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mother characters have other dimensions (jobs, cultures, hobbies, personality traits) and are not defined solely by being mothers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include both pleasures and difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Pregnancy contains moments of joy (feeling movement, first breath) as well as difficulty; media often flattens one side or the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance scenes to show what is wonderful (e.g., fetal movement, taking first breath) alongside discomforts and fears, so portrayals feel rounded and human.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent motherhood across cultural and social contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Motherhood and pregnancy experiences vary across cultures and diasporas; representation should reflect that diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural specifics (Vietnamese-French diaspora example) and avoid assuming a single cultural norm; draw on varied backgrounds for authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research period/medical specifics for historical settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical childbirth practices and limitations (e.g., 19th-century medicine, postpartum hemorrhage, primitive treatments like 'packing the wound with moss') matter for plausibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing period settings, consult historical medical sources to find complications and realistic remedies; be aware that some complications in earlier eras often had fatal outcomes unless you introduce plausible mitigating factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mundane authenticity rather than extremes only
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction often shows either catastrophic pregnancy outcomes or perfectly smooth ones; everyday messy reality is underrepresented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage 'little problems' and daily lived details to convey authenticity — this often reads truer than oscillation between extremes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show mothers and children in ordinary places
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing mothers and children in ordinary settings (e.g., toddlers in a pirate captain's cabin) can be refreshing and realistic because such scenes are rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include domestic or background parenting moments in settings where writers typically omit them to signal a lived-in world and increase representation.
